chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from his father, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was brought a man who had killed a man by error. So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Who is your clan and your relatives?' He said, 'I have no clan nor relatives in this city.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So from which of the cities are you?' He said, 'I am a man from the people of Mosul, born in it, and I have relatives and a family there.'

He said: So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) inquired about him, but did not find for him any relatives or clan in Kufa. He said: So he wrote to his governor in Mosul: 'As for after, so-and-so son of so-and-so, and his appearance is such and such, killed a man from the Muslims by error. He mentioned that he is a man from Mosul, and that he has relatives and a family there. And I have sent him to you with my messenger, so-and-so son of so-and-so, and his appearance is such and such. So when he comes to you, God willing, and you read my letter, investigate his matter and ask about his relatives from the Muslims.'

If he is from the people of Mosul, from those born in it, and you find for him relatives among the Muslims there, gather them to you. Then look: if there is among them a man who inherits him, having a share in the Book (Quran), whom no one from his relatives bars from his inheritance, then obligate him the blood money (diya) and take it from him in installments over three years.

If there is not among his relatives anyone who has a share in the Book, and his relatives are equal in lineage, and he has relatives from his father and his mother equal in lineage, then distribute the blood money upon his relatives from his father and upon his relatives from his mother, from the adult Muslim males. Then assign two-thirds of the blood money upon his relatives from his father, and one-third upon his relatives from his mother.

And if he has no relatives from his father, then distribute the blood money upon his relatives from his mother, from the adult Muslim males. Then seize them with it and make them pay the blood money over three years.

If he has no relatives from his mother nor any relatives from his father, then distribute the blood money upon the people of Mosul, from those born in it and raised there, and do not include others among them from the people of the city. Then collect that from them over three years, an installment each year, until you have fully collected it, God willing.

And if so-and-so son of so-and-so has no relatives from the people of Mosul, nor is he from its people, and he has falsified it, then return him to me with my messenger, so-and-so son of so-and-so, God willing. For I am his guardian and the one who pays on his behalf, and I will not invalidate the blood of a Muslim man.

key_terms.دِيَة: Blood money or compensation paid for homicide or injury
key_terms.نُجُوماً: Installments (plural of najm, referring to a specific portion or installment)

ai.seo_question: Who is responsible for paying blood money if the killer has no relatives?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the hierarchical distribution of blood money (diya) for accidental homicide, emphasizing the Imam’s role in verifying lineage and ensuring justice. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that the Imam acts as the guardian (wali) for those without known kin, preventing the forfeiture of a Muslim’s life due to lack of identifiable relatives. The text also highlights the practical administration of diya through installment payments ('najm') over three years, a detail significant in fiqh discussions on liquidity and social welfare.
